newsitem.title: USA: PartnerRe considers purchase of SAFR.
newsitem.headline: PartnerRe considers purchase of SAFR.

text.p: PartnerRe Ltd said on Wednesday it had reached an understanding with Swiss Reinsurance Co that gives it the opportunity to consider the purchase of Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR), a European reinsurer based in Paris.
Swiss Re announced in Europe on Wednesday that it intended to buy the 78 percent of SAFR it did not already own.
Swiss Re agreed to buy 57 percent of SAFR from Centrale des Assurances Generales de France and Athena, a unit of Worms et Cie, for $543 million.
Swiss Re also announced it will offer to buy the 21 percent of the SAFR shares owned by the public, PartnerRe said.
Although it is subject to negotiation, PartnerRe said it currently expects the consideration to Swiss Re would consist of a combination of cash and PartnerRe common stock.
Swiss Re currently owns 11 percent of PartnerRe's outstanding shares, or 19 percent assuming the exercise of the Class A Warrants held by Swiss Re.

In no event would Swiss Re's holdings in PartnerRe after such transaction exceed 21 percent of PartnerRe's outstanding shares, or 27 percent assuming the exercise of the class A warrants, PartnerRe said.
PartnerRe said discussions are expected to be concluded by March 31 and said it does not expect to make any further announcements or release any additional information prior to that date.

"We are delighted to be in a position to assess all possible synergies between PartnerRe and SAFR, which is a high-quality reinsurer we know well and respect," PartnerRe chief executive Herbert Haag said.

"While we shall maintain our specialization as a catastrophe reinsurer, we believe that a combined operation could significantly diversify our portfolio, both in terms of geography and lines of business, and expand our global market presence through the establishment of valuable new client relationships," he said.

"Our assessment will focus on identifying those opportunities where SAFR's expertise and established infrastructure would be complementary to our specialty operation which could translate into enhanced shareholder value through cross-selling opportunities and more efficient capital utilization," he said.
SAFR, founded in 1884, is an important European direct reinsurer, PartnerRe said.

Its gross premiums for 1995 totaled 4.139 billion French francs (US $731 million) of which 32 percent originated from France, 43 percent from the rest of Europe, 12 percent from Asia and 13 percent from other countries including North America.
SAFR writes both life and non-life business and in 1995 recorded profits of 320 million francs (US $57 million).

Partner Re Ltd. provides, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Partner Reinsurance Company Ltd., catastrophe reinsurance to insurance companies on a worldwide basis. Risks reinsured include windstorm, earthquake, floods, fires and explosions.
